# Rank Transform of an Array.

@example The different values in order are -3, 8 and 15; both 15s get rank 3.
[15,-3,15,8]
=> [3,1,3,2]

@example Both 3s get rank 1, and 5, the next value up, gets rank 2, not 3.
[7,3,3,5]
=> [3,1,1,2]

@example An empty array has nothing to rank.
[]
=> []

# A single element.
[42]
=> [1]

# All elements equal.
[-5,-5,-5,-5]
=> [1,1,1,1]

# Ties at the smallest value, in the middle and at the largest value, in
# no particular order.
[10,-1,7,4,-1,10,7]
=> [4,1,3,2,1,4,3]

# A tie of three, then of two: no gaps after either.
[8,8,8,2,2,5]
=> [3,3,3,1,1,2]

# Already ascending, and descending.
[-2,0,3,8,11]
=> [1,2,3,4,5]

[9,6,3,0,-3]
=> [5,4,3,2,1]

# Zero between negative and positive values.
[0,-1,1,0]
=> [2,1,3,2]

# The extremes.
[1000000000,-1000000000,0]
=> [3,1,2]

[1000000000,1000000000,-1000000000]
=> [2,2,1]

[-1000000000,-999999999,-1000000000]
=> [1,2,1]

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[-3,0]
=> [1,2]

@gen 2 small
[-1000000000,-3,2,-3,-3,-1,0]
=> [1,2,5,2,2,3,4]

@gen 3 small
[2,-3,1,-2,3]
=> [4,1,3,2,5]

@gen 4 small
[3]
=> [1]

@gen 5 small
[-2,2,-3]
=> [2,3,1]

@gen 6 small
[1,-3,-3]
=> [2,1,1]
